text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Broker McIntosh Baring has compiled an international survey which finds that Australian banks are among the most profitable in the world, with their shareholders enjoying the highest dividend payouts. The survey compares 40 banks across six countries and shows only British banks are more profitable than Australian ones. Page 1.

Opposition Transport Minister Lindsay Tanner has written to Federal Finance Minister John Fahey calling for public release of the full details of the regulatory regime and assessment criteria for the sale of airports in order to avoid a repeat of the tendering process for the Victorian casino licence. Page 3.

The Labor Party and the Coalition were accusing each other of economic incompetence over the proposed A$7.3 billion in cuts to the government's deficit reduction programmess, with Prime Minister John Howard claiming the blocking of budget measures would advesely affect interest rates. Page 4.

Woodside Petroleum Ltd has hit a big gas reservoir in the Lynx 1 wildcat well in the North West Shelf area, which could see the company reaching its goal of proving up gas reserves of 35 trillion cubic feet. Page 19.

An information package for members of the Australian Stock Exchange was launched yesterday by chairman Maurice Newman. The campaign for the demutualisation of the exchange will be pushed Australia-wide, being sent to 92 broking firms and 522 individual ASX members this morning. Page 19.

After reporting a modest net profit for the year to June 30, NRMA Insurance will concentrate on controlling its expenses, according to chief executive Malcolm Jones. The general insurance group reported a profit of A$900,000 compared to a loss of A$6.5 million in the previous year, while the NRMA Group result was A$8.8 million compared with a $62.7 million loss the year before. Page 20.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian Stock Exchange yesterday released a blueprint for its demutualisation, which revealed financial institutions will be denied the opportunity to access its proposed share allocation. The blueprint outlined the benefits and perceived disadvanages of abandoning the mutual structure. Page 17.

The New South Wales Premier's Office yesterday confirmed it will make an announcement today on the major Newcrest Mining Ltd A$440 million Cadia Hill copper-gold project in the state's central west following a commission of inquiry report. It is expected the development will be approved. Page 17.

Australian Stock Exchange managing director Richard Humphry indicated yesterday the exchange's creative proposal to demutualise and list its shares on its own exchange had attracted interest from other world bourses. Page 17.

On the eve of the Wallis inquiry submissions deadline, Anne Lamont, former policy director with Canada's Office of the System of Financial Institutions, said a mega-regulator of financial services is the best option in a rapidly evolving market. The inquiry committee will travel to Canada this week to examine the operation of a mega-regulator system. Page 17.

MIM Holdings Ltd chief executive Nick Stump says the company will be unable to decide whether or not it will remain a major force in the zinc and lead industry until the viability of the George Fisher orebody in northern Queensland is known. Page 19.

CSIRO chief executive Dr Malcolm McIntosh said the Co-operative Research Centre for Landscape Evolution and Mineral Exploration was negotiating with Joseph Gutnick's diamond exploration arm Astro Mining NL to use his exploration technology, which discovered West Australian gold mines, to search for diamonds. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Australian Stock Exchange yesterday revealed sweeping changes to its ownership structure, moving it closer to its A$150 million sharemarket listing. The demutualisation scheme, modelled on similar schemes undertaken by exchanges in Europe, will see any individual, institution, and/or company able to operate as a broker to buy and sell shares. Page 31.

Documents obtained by the Herald indicate that John Bertrand's Southern Cross syndicate, which competed for the 1994 America's Cup yacht race, was unable to satisfy the Tax Concession Committee that its expenditure on research and development was eligiblefor tax breaks. Page 31.

Institutional shareholders are placing pressure on Mayne Nickless to hand over its entire A$1.2 billion stake in Optus Communications in the coming entitlement issue, going against the wishes of the organisers of the Optus float who are relying on Mayne to retain some of its 500 million shares and provide them as some of the new shares for the sharemarket listing. Page 31.

An Australian Bureau of Statistics report on managed funds has found growth in assets last financial year of nine percent to A$317 billion, yet the level of deposits by residents in banks grew at a stronger rate of 11 per cent, dismissing bankers' fears hat their deposit base is being snaffled by fund managers. Page 33.

Science and Technology Minister Peter McGauran said yesterday that Opposition plans to block A$1.9 billion in cuts to the research and development concession scheme were irresponsible, considering that 90 percent of Australian research would continue regrdless. McGauran vowed the hovernment would not make cuts elsewhere in the science portfolio if the Senate blocked the measures. Page 33.

Stockbroking firm McIntosh Corporate's annual survey of equity capital raising activity showed the call for equity capital is expected to fall by as much as 6.6 percent to about A$15 billion in the current financial year because of a more subdued demand by overseas investors. Page 33.
THE AGE
The Australian Stock Exchange is pressing ahead with its push to demutualise, yesterday publishing an "independent" report backing its plans as the best way to meet future competition. Page C1.
Plutonic Resources is fighting to regain control of two potentially valuable mining leases near its flagship WG gold mine that were accidentally surrendered because of a clerical error. Page C1.

The official August VFACTS figures indicate the battle for market leadership in the motor industry is heating up, confirming Holden has won five out of eight months of the year, but it is still 325 vehicles behind Ford in the race for annual No. 1. Page C2.

Amcor chief executive Don Macfarlane yesterday warned of job losses ahead and said the first-half profits at the paper and packaging group would be down on last time. Macfarlane said the group, in attempting to offset the intense pricing pressures in the Australian market, would step up its restructuring programme to recover pricing margins lost through the reduction in tariffs. Page C3.

Energy Resources of Australia chief executive Phil Shirvington commented yesterday on a study of the world uranium market by the London-based Uranium Institute, saying Australia can supply an extra 7,000 tonnes of uranium a year by the turn of the century, almost trebling output. Page C3.

Mayne Nickless is under pressure from its institutional shareholders to hand over all of its A$1.2 billion stake in Optus Communications in the coming entitlement issue. However, the company's largest shareholders have been pushing the group's management to reserve all of the shares to ensure their access to Optus. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
